details: The package's install hook runs node index.js, which loads lib/core.js. On install, core.js collects the local username, hostname, current working directory, and a Unix timestamp, encodes them into the DNS query name "srmods.<username>.<hostname>.<cwd>.<timestamp>.oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz", and issues a DNS resolution request to that name, exfiltrating host metadata to the attacker-controlled domain oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz. The package's exported financial-workflow modules (withdraw/orders/payments) are a decoy facade; the real behaviour is the install-time DNS beacon. The package's install script (node index.js) runs an obfuscated beacon on install. It reads the OS username, hostname, and current working directory, then encodes them with a timestamp into a DNS query of the form srmods.<user>.<host>.<cwd>.<ts>.oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz and resolves it via dns.resolve4, exfiltrating host metadata to the attacker-controlled domain oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz. The beacon loads the os and dns modules through module.constructor._load to bypass the standard require chain, and the package bundles benign-looking financial-workflow modules as a decoy.
